summary: This article explains what different teeth do, how bacteria, sugar, and acid cause cavities, and the daily habits, foods, and dentist visits that keep teeth healthy, including the traditional miswak.
introduce: Write “Alike” and “Different” at the top of a T-chart on the board and ask students to compare two school subjects in one minute. Explain that “Healthy Teeth for Life” asks them to make the same kind of comparison.

keyTerms.def: tiny living things that can only be seen with a microscope
a sour liquid that can slowly eat away at some materials
a wide tooth at the back of the mouth used for grinding food

challengeTerms.def: lasting for a very long time or forever
a natural, solid substance, such as calcium, found in rocks and in the body
to wear something away slowly, little by little

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that brushing your teeth is more important than what you eat and drink? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how a cavity forms and two ways to prevent one.
struggling: Pre-teach bacteria, acid, and molar with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers fill in a T-chart of alike and different with sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses permanent, mineral, and erode to compare two ideas from the article and explain which difference matters most.
